definition: The latent diffusion model (LDM) is a diffusion model architecture developed by the CompVis (Computer Vision & Learning) group at LMU Munich.
details: Introduced in 2015, diffusion models (DMs) are trained with the objective of removing successive applications of noise (commonly Gaussian) on training images. The LDM is an improvement on standard DM by performing diffusion modeling in a latent space, and by allowing self-attention and cross-attention conditioning. LDMs are widely used in practical diffusion models. For instance, Stable Diffusion versions 1.1 to 2.1 were based on the LDM architecture.

explainer.lead: The latent diffusion model is a diffusion architecture from the CompVis group at LMU Munich that performs diffusion modelling in a latent space. It matters because it made diffusion practical and underpins widely used image generators.

tiers.eli5: Rather than cleaning up a huge smudged picture pixel by pixel, you first shrink it to a small sketch, clean the sketch, and blow it back up. It is faster and the results still look good.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run the noise-removal process in a compressed latent space and add self-attention and cross-attention conditioning. It is the standard recipe behind many practical diffusion models, not a niche variant.
